title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, and Upgrade/Rollback
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview

This document is a consolidated deployment and operational reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers reference architectures, on-prem packaging requirements, pre-deployment customer requirements, day-2 operational runbooks, and upgrade/rollback procedures. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, customer engineers, and solutions architects.

Key goals
- Provide repeatable, testable deployment steps that teams and customers can follow.
- Define minimum hardware, networking, and security requirements.
- Document day-2 operations (monitoring, scaling, backups, incident escalation).
- Provide safe, reversible upgrade and rollback procedures with verification checks.

Contents (top-level)
1) Pre-deployment customer requirements and checklist
2) Reference architectures (VPC and on-prem)
3) On-prem packaging and installation notes (air-gapped options)
4) Day-2 operations: monitoring, backups, runbooks, common failures
5) Upgrade and rollback procedure (canary and full-rollout)
6) Appendix: sample manifests, commands, and contact/ownership

1) Pre-deployment customer requirements and checklist

Short intro: Before scheduling a deployment or providing on-prem artifacts, confirm the customer meets the following requirements. This reduces failed installs and speeds time-to-first-inference.

Customer checklist (must be provided by customer):
- Point of contact (POC) for networking, storage, and security: name/email/phone.
- Network design diagram (CIDR blocks, subnets, route tables, NAT/GW, firewall rules).
- Administrative access method: jumpbox SSH/RDP or bastion (IP allowlist).
- KMS/HSM details for key management and whether customer will provide encryption keys.
- Desired deployment mode: VPC-hosted (customer-managed cloud account) or on-prem (rack/VMs or air-gapped).
- Estimated peak qps, average request size, typical sequence length, concurrency targets (for capacity sizing).
- Compliance requirements (PCI, HIPAA, SOC2) and any required audit log retention windows.

Minimum required information table (customer -> Redwood mapping):
| Item | Example / Format | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Control plane endpoint | https://control.example.corp | Redwood remote management (if allowed) |
| Admin CIDR | 10.40.0.0/24 | Who can reach management interfaces |
| GPU hosts | 4 x A100 80GB or equivalent | Capacity planning |
| Storage | NFS or Ceph, 10 TB usable | Model artifacts, persistent state |
| KMS | AWS KMS / Vault HSM | Encryption of credentials and keys |

Security & compliance pre-reqs
- TLS termination: terminate at customer load balancer or Redwood ingress depending on policy.
- PKI: customer must provide TLS certs for production endpoints or authorize Redwood CA for short-lived certs.
- RBAC: provide LDAP/AD details for SSO integration if required.
- Audit logging: S3/ELK/other endpoints for log export.

2) Reference architectures

A. VPC-hosted (customer cloud account) reference architecture\- Summary: This is the recommended path for customers who want isolation but wish to run infrastructure in their cloud account (AWS, GCP, Azure). Redwood provides terraform modules and AMIs/VM images.

Key components and services:
- Management VPC: small control-plane components (if using Redwood-managed control-plane) or customer-run control-plane.
- Data plane VPCs: GPU worker subnets, autoscaling groups, node pools.
- Private NLB/ALB for ingress, with customer-managed certs at ACM (AWS).
- S3-compatible artifact store (customer S3 or MinIO).
- KMS integration for secrets and model encryption.

Network flow summary:
1) Customer app -> Private NLB (TLS) -> Ingress -> Router -> Model worker pool.
2) Workers contact artifact store & key management endpoints over private endpoints.

SLOs and deployment targets (typical):
- Latency (99th): configurable per-customer, typical SLO 200ms for small generation payloads, 1s for long-form generation.
- Availability: target 99.95% for Dedicated capacity mode.

B. On-prem (air-gapped and connected) reference architecture\- Summary: For regulated customers requiring no external network egress. Provide an air-gapped packaging option with an offline installer and signed artifacts.

Key components:
- Front-door load balancer (F5/HAProxy)
- Management VM cluster (control plane) - can be isolated VMs or Kubernetes cluster with restricted egress.
- GPU cluster (bare-metal or virtualized) with NVLink/IB networking where available.
- Storage: NFS/Gluster/Ceph with encryption at rest.
- Optional jumpbox for support access.

Packaging notes for air-gapped installs:
- Deliverables: signed tarball of container images (OCI layout), offline helm charts, schema for YAML manifests, and a SHA256-signed manifest file.
- Installation artifact verification: md5/sha256 checksums and GPG signatures.

3) On-prem packaging and installation notes

Supported platforms and minimal versions:
- Kubernetes: 1.24+ (tested 1.25 and 1.26).
- Docker/containerd: containerd 1.6+, Docker Engine 20.10+.
- Linux: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, RHEL 8.x, Rocky 8.x.
- GPU drivers: NVIDIA driver 525+ and CUDA 11.8+ for A100; verify compatibility matrix in the artifacts README.

Package contents (example):
- artifacts/ (OCI tar archives for all containers)
- charts/ (Helm charts: control-plane, ingress, router, worker)
- manifests/ (example YAMLs for CRDs and default configs)
- install.sh (offline installer script)
- checksums.txt (sha256), signatures.asc (GPG signed)

Installation pre-checks (run before install):
1) Verify kernel & driver: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version --format=csv`
2) Verify storage mounts: `df -h` and ensure model-store mount point has correct permissions.
3) Validate ports: management (8443), telemetry (9100/9090), grpc (50051) must be reachable internally.

Example install sequence (air-gapped):
1) Copy artifacts to installer host and validate checksums.
2) Run `sudo ./install.sh --mode airgap --config customer-config.yaml`.
3) Wait for control-plane pods to reach READY state: `kubectl -n rwi get pods -o wide`
4) Validate worker registration in control plane UI or via CLI: `rwictl status`

4) Day-2 operations: monitoring, backups, runbooks, common failures

Monitoring & observability
- Required telemetry: node exporter, cAdvisor, Prometheus, Grafana dashboards, Loki (logs), and Tempo (traces) for request flows.
- Suggested dashboards: per-model latency breakdown, per-worker GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, request QPS, error rates (5xx/4xx).
- Alerts (example thresholds):
  - GPU memory pressure: warning at 70%, critical at 90%.
  - Pod restart rate: >5 restarts in 10m -> Pager.
  - KV cache miss ratio > 30% for sustained 10m -> Investigate cache priming.
  - 99th percentile latency > configured SLO for 15m -> Pager and automatic fallback to cheaper model variant.

Backups and artifact retention
- Model artifacts should be replicated to an offsite S3-compatible bucket or a customer-provided backup target nightly.
- Control-plane DB (Postgres) daily snapshot and WAL archiving with 30-day retention default.
- Secrets (KMS) should be backed by customer key-policy and rotation schedule.

Common operational runbooks (short form)
- Worker OOM / Pod eviction
  1) Check `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl logs` for OOM messages.
  2) Confirm GPU memory utilization with `nvidia-smi`.
  3) If caused by unexpectedly large prompts, apply request size limit via ingress policy and restart worker.

- High latency on 99th percentile
  1) Check recent rollout/config changes: `kubectl get deploy -o wide` and `/control-plane/rollouts`.
  2) Inspect batch sizes and queue length on router.
  3) If saturation, scale worker pool (manual): `kubectl scale --replicas=<N> deployment/worker-pool`.

- Lost connectivity to artifact store
  1) Verify mount health and NFS server.
  2) Fallback to local cached model if available: enable `model_cache_local=true` in control-plane config and restart router.

Escalation matrix (short)
- Tier 1: Customer on-call / SRE (first 30 minutes)
- Tier 2: Redwood Customer Engineering (30-120 minutes)
- Tier 3: Redwood Serve/RTE on-call (120+ minutes)

5) Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles
- Use canary-first upgrades for control-plane and router.
- Ensure automated health checks and synthetic request verification before promoting.
- All upgrades must be reversible with a documented rollback play.

Pre-upgrade checklist
- Validate backup of control-plane DB and snapshot artifacts.
- Ensure capacity headroom of at least 20% for brief scaling needs.
- Review release notes for breaking changes and operator alerts.

Canary upgrade procedure (recommended)
1) Create a canary namespace or node pool: `kubectl apply -f canary-ns.yaml`
2) Deploy new control-plane image to canary: `kubectl set image deployment/control-plane control-plane=registry.example.com/rwi/control-plane:vX.Y.Z -n canary`
3) Run automated smoke tests (use `rwictl test smoke --endpoint https://canary.example`): must pass 100% for 10m.
4) Monitor metrics for error spikes and latency for 30m.
5) If stable, promote by slowly rolling to production groups using phased rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable windows).

Rollback procedure (if canary or rollout fails)
1) Immediately stop rollout: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/control-plane`
2) Roll back to last-known-good revision: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane --to-revision=<rev>`
3) Revert any config changes applied during upgrade (feature flags, ingress rules).
4) Run verification smoke tests in production traffic shadowing mode for 15m.
5) Open incident with RCA ownership assigned and schedule postmortem.

Emergency rollback (fast path)
- If production is severely impacted (SLO breaches, data corruption risk), execute emergency rollback script: `./emergency-rollback.sh --component control-plane --target-revision=<rev>` (this script automates DB restore from snapshot and redeploy). Only CI/CD or authorized SREs should run this; ensure audit logging is enabled.

Validation and post-upgrade checks
- Synthetic test suite must run and report 0 failed critical tests.
- Confirm model serving correctness by running sample prompts from the customer-provided test set and comparing checksums / similarity metrics.
- Confirm telemetry ingestion and retention for the new version.

6) Appendix: sample manifests, commands, and ownership

Sample `rwictl` commands
- `rwictl status --json` (returns cluster status)
- `rwictl model list` (lists models & versions)
- `rwictl logs --component worker --since 1h`

Sample Kubernetes snippet (worker deployment):
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: worker-pool
  namespace: rwi
spec:
  replicas: 4
  template:
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        accelerator: nvidia
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: registry.example.com/rwi/worker:vX.Y.Z
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
          requests:
            cpu: "2000m"
            memory: "24Gi"
```
